clue.text: Boss of firm that's always in the black?

definitions.text: Boss of firm that's always in the black?

parts.words: Boss of firm that's always in the black?
parts.note: a firm always in the black sounds solvent, but here it is one whose staff always wear black mourning clothes: an undertaker's business

explanation.surface: Praise for a chief executive whose company never runs at a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the black' means in profit in business talk; read literally it is the black worn at funerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an undertaking business, whose staff dress in mourning black, is the person who arranges funerals.

clue.text: Bombast in opera put off a man

indicators.note: to put something off is to remove it, so the letter given by the next word is dropped from the opera

parts.note: Faust is Gounod's opera
the letter A, as written
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man is turned away from a performance of an opera because of its pompous language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' removes A from FAUST, leaving FUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Fustian is a word for pompous, inflated language, the same thing as bombast.

clue.text: Family girl smuggles drug into French resort

indicators.note: the drug goes into the resort, so its letter sits inside that town's name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is short for ecstasy

explanation.surface: A young relative is caught bringing narcotics into a Riviera town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggles' just carries the surface; 'into' puts E inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a girl in one's family, the daughter of a sibling.

clue.text: Feature of war and tumult involving one's own family

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap round, so the tumult encloses the family

parts.note: a riot is a tumult
one's own flesh and blood means one's family

explanation.surface: War and civil disorder drag in a person's relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature of war' is a sound or sight of battle; 'one's own family' comes from the phrase 'one's own flesh and blood'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunfire from rifles is a typical sound and sight of warfare.

clue.text: Willingly following to end of biography

indicators.note: the letter for following is shifted to the end of the biography word

parts.note: a life is a biography
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone happily reads on to the last page of a life story.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving F in LIFE to the end gives LIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Lief is an old word meaning gladly or willingly, as in 'I would as lief stay'.

clue.text: Musical genre almost needs special language, one points out

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the genre loses its final letter

parts.note: indie is a genre of music
cant is the jargon of a particular group

explanation.surface: A style of music is said to require its own jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of INDIE, giving INDI.
explanation.definitionFit: An indicant is something that indicates, i.e. a thing that points something out.

clue.text: Put down gong journalist collects

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the journalist encloses the gong

parts.note: ED, editor, is the crossword journalist
gong is slang for a medal or honour, such as the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: A reporter picks up an honour and is told to put down a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' here means set firmly in place, not belittle; MBE is a British honour often called a gong.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly down in a surrounding mass, to set it in place.

clue.text: Unreliable third earl presenting a number of faces

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be depended on to stay put, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An untrustworthy aristocrat, third holder of his title, is two-faced or worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unreliable' rearranges THIRD EARL.
explanation.definitionFit: Trihedral describes a solid figure having three plane faces, a particular number of faces.

clue.text: Material left I reused somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recycles the leftover stuff in some way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I and REUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is whatever material remains after the rest has been removed or used.

clue.text: Protection when English females enter city

indicators.note: the letters for English and females go inside the word for protection

parts.note: a shield gives protection
F is short for female; doubled, FF stands for females

explanation.surface: Safety measures are arranged when a group of English women arrive in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enter' places EFF inside SHIELD: SH-EFF-IELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.

clue.text: Taunts cricketers — one gets caught

indicators.note: a thing that gets caught is held within, so the numeral sits inside the cricketers

parts.note: bats are batsmen in cricket
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fielders jeer when one batsman is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets caught' puts I inside BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to taunt or tease them, so baits matches taunts as verbs.

clue.text: Salesfolk cold-calling in America?

parts.note: cold-calling looks like unsolicited phoning, but here it means doorstep sellers of something cold, delivering blocks of it in the US

explanation.surface: A comment on pushy telephone salespeople in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: American usage names a man who delivered blocks of ice for iceboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US an iceman is a tradesman who sold and delivered ice to homes.

clue.text: A man leading detectives is drug user!

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
the man leading is the head, the one in charge

explanation.surface: A man in charge of the detective squad turns out to be on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A, then the CID, then its HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidhead is slang for a habitual taker of LSD, a drug user.

clue.text: US city politician has lost heart to pretty girls

parts.note: NY is New York
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A New York politician has lost his nerve in front of attractive women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost heart' takes the middle A out of HAS, leaving HS.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology nymphs are beautiful young maidens, so the word is used loosely for pretty girls.

clue.text: What could show dray to be adequate for the job?

definitions.text: to be adequate for the job

parts.note: a yard is a measure; written upwards in a down entry it reads as this word for a brewer's cart

explanation.surface: A question about whether a brewer's cart is fit for its work.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, a measure (YARD) going up, gives DRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure up is an idiom meaning to reach the required standard, to be good enough.

clue.text: Like town with inadequate resources for posse?

definitions.text: Like town with inadequate resources for posse?

parts.words: Like town with inadequate resources for posse?
parts.note: a small backward place is described by an idiom; a Western sheriff's posse would need many mounts, but this place has a single steed

explanation.surface: A Wild West settlement lacks the means to send riders after outlaws.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a small, insignificant town is taken literally: it owns only one mount.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is an idiom for a small, dull place with few facilities.

clue.text: Hi, sir! — cute unconventional classroom style?

indicators.note: unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil greets a teacher cheekily, a novel approach to lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' rearranges HI SIR CUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A heuristic teaching method lets pupils discover things for themselves, a style of instruction.

clue.text: Malevolent archdeacon, little old creature coming to premature end

parts.note: Ven. (Venerable) is the title of an archdeacon
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: ending early means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a mouse is a small creature

explanation.surface: A spiteful churchman's small pet dies young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to premature end' cuts the E from MOUSE, giving MOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous is used figuratively for spiteful or full of malice.

clue.text: Listen to row becoming less inhibited?

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Hearing an argument makes someone loosen up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartier means more hearty: more boisterous and unrestrained in manner.

clue.text: Reception area for travellers — feature introduced by boss

indicators.note: being introduced by the boss means going inside that word

parts.note: a head is a boss
the lip is a facial feature

explanation.surface: The chief brings in a new feature for the hotel's arrivals lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced by' puts LIP into HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A helipad is a landing area where helicopter passengers arrive.

clue.text: With this stuff you get friend to massage back

indicators.note: back means read the other way, so both words are turned round

parts.note: pal means friend
to rub is to massage

explanation.surface: Get a mate to give you a back rub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PALRUB round.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlap is a coarse fabric of jute or hemp, the material referred to as this stuff.

clue.text: Craft shown by very religious rascal

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very religious
a rogue is a rascal

explanation.surface: A boat displayed by a devout scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirogue is a dugout canoe, a type of small boat or craft.

clue.text: Old penny buried in our soil mistaken for foreign coin

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside the other letters
mistaken means wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for a penny in old British money

explanation.surface: An ancient coin dug up in the garden is wrongly identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges OUR SOIL to LOUISOR, and 'buried in' sets D among those letters, after LOUIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The louis d'or was a gold coin of pre-revolutionary France.

clue.text: Country paper includes upsetting notice

indicators.note: a paper that includes something has it inside

parts.note: The Sun is a British newspaper

indicators.note: upsetting a word in a down entry turns it upside down, i.e. reverses it

parts.note: an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: A national newspaper carries a disturbing announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns AD upside down, as fits a down entry, giving DA; The Sun is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Bloke felt absence of woman, as East ender said

indicators.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops the h, so the phrase is pronounced that way

parts.note: felt the absence of a woman is missed her

explanation.surface: A man pined for his wife, as a Londoner put it.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney says 'missed her' as 'missed 'er', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mister is used, often in address, for a man, a bloke.

clue.text: Material wife kept in drawer

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the wife's letter is placed within the drawer

parts.note: a till is a cash drawer

explanation.surface: Fabric that the wife stores in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture; it is a cash register.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ribs.

clue.text: Gladly pass out — time to go

indicators.note: to go means to be dropped, so the letter for time leaves

parts.note: to faint is to pass out

explanation.surface: Someone would happily faint, but it's time to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Fain is an archaic word for gladly or willingly.

clue.text: Argue quietly, gaining dominance

parts.note: p (piano) means quietly in music
a lead is a position of dominance

explanation.surface: Someone makes a case softly and still comes out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to argue a case, especially in court.

clue.text: Under control but left dangling?

definitions.meaning: under someone's control, manipulated like a puppet
literally hanging from a cord, or kept waiting in suspense

explanation.definitionFit: A puppet on a cord is both controlled and hanging, giving the idiom for being kept dependent or in suspense.

clue.text: Phil had son involved with dance — ballet!

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Phil's boy got caught up in dancing and joined the ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges PHIL HAD SON with DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravel's work of this name, about two young lovers, is a ballet.
